title: Fearlessness first
hookLine: Krishna's list of divine qualities starts with fearlessness, for an Arjuna who dropped his bow
carry: fearlessness is the first divine quality

cards: Go back to where the Gita began. Arjuna stands in his chariot between two armies and sees his teachers, cousins and uncles on the other side.
His limbs give way, his mouth goes dry, his great bow Gandiva slips from his hand, and he sinks down, overcome with grief.
Fifteen chapters later, Krishna gives him a list: the qualities of someone born to a divine inheritance. And the very first word, before truth, before compassion, is abhaya. Fearlessness.

teach.b: Verses one to three are one long sentence. Fearlessness. Purity of heart.
Steadiness in knowledge and practice. Giving. Self-control.
Straightness. Then: doing no harm, truth, freedom from anger, letting go, peace, not gossiping about others, kindness to all beings, not being greedy, gentleness, modesty, not being fickle.
And to close: energy, forgiveness, endurance, cleanliness, no malice, no excess pride. Twenty-six in all. Krishna calls them daivi sampad, the divine inheritance, like a fortune you're born into.
Why fearlessness first? The text doesn't say. One answer teachers give: without it, the others don't hold.
It's hard to tell the truth if you're afraid, hard to forgive, to give, to stay gentle. Fear quietly bends everything else.
The second word, sattva-samshuddhi, purity of heart, is about what's underneath: clean motives, not only clean hands. Together they make today's line.

Verse four gives the opposite list, briefly: hypocrisy, arrogance, too much pride, anger, harshness and ignorance. Tomorrow, that side. Verse five: the divine inheritance leads to freedom, the other to bondage.
Then Krishna turns to Arjuna, who began this whole conversation overcome with grief, and says something gentle: do not grieve, Arjuna.
You were born to the divine inheritance. The inheritance is already his.
That's the teaching: in Hinduism, fearlessness isn't toughness. It grows from knowing who you are, the self that, as chapter two said, no weapon can cut.
It's why so many images of the gods show one palm raised toward you: abhaya mudra, the gesture that says, do not fear.

how: Some Hindu teachers use Gita 16.1–16.3 as a list of virtues to cultivate, opening with abhaya (fearlessness); many murtis and images of the gods show abhaya mudra, the raised open palm that says 'do not fear'.

o: fearlessness, the first of the divine qualities
bravado, acting tough so no one sees you're scared

Krishna tells Arjuna he was born to the divine inheritance

games.q: Krishna has listed the divine and the demonic qualities. Arjuna, who began the Gita overcome with grief, is listening. what does Krishna say to him?
o: watch out: you have the demonic ones.
do not grieve: you were born to the divine inheritance.
you must earn these before you fight.
games.why: do not grieve. verse 5 is a reassurance, not a warning.

practice: Picture an image of a Hindu god with the right palm raised toward you, abhaya mudra: do not fear. Then find one small fear you're carrying, a conversation you're avoiding, and hold it in front of that open hand.
Breathe in and feel where it sits; breathe out and let it soften. If you pray, ask for courage; if you don't, ask quietly: if this fear were smaller, what would I do?

wordCard.voice: Abhaya, fearlessness, no fear. Gita sixteen, one to five: the first of twenty-six qualities of the divine inheritance, daivi sampad, alongside purity of heart.

orig.note: Sanskrit: abhaya, fearlessness (a + bhaya, no fear); the first of the divine qualities in Gita 16.1.

carryVoice: Your line: fearlessness is the first divine quality. Courage first, a clean heart underneath. Day two hundred thirteen, in the books.
